stem: A 10-month-old child is using one hand predominantly when playing with toys. If a child declares themselves left- or right-handed in the first 6–12 months, what should you do?

options.text: Consider whether the child has cerebral palsy and look for other evidence of this in the child
Reassure his/her mother that this is normal development
Request nerve conduction studies to look for a peripheral neuropathy
Send the child to an occupational therapist for treatment of their motor dyspraxia

explanation: Early hand preference in infancy is abnormal and should prompt assessment for an underlying neurological cause, particularly cerebral palsy with unilateral motor signs.
rationale: The case describes asymmetrical tone, brisk reflexes, clonus, and unilateral weakness, all consistent with hemiplegic cerebral palsy. Early hand preference in infancy is a red flag for this.

optionExplanations.A: Correct. Early handedness can be a sign of unilateral upper motor neuron dysfunction; examine for hemiplegic cerebral palsy and associated findings.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect. Hand preference before 12 months is not usually normal development and should not be dismissed.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect. Peripheral neuropathy would not be the usual first consideration for early hand preference with upper motor neuron signs.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect. Motor dyspraxia is not the main concern here; the pattern suggests a focal neurological deficit requiring medical assessment.

Instructions

Question 9 - 12 relate to this case

Case 4

A mother brings her 10 month old child to see you because her son is mostly using his left hand to play with toys and she is not sure if this is just because he is going to be left handed. He is otherwise growing well and is a happy child. The child was born at 35 weeks with a birth weight of 3.1 kg. He was breastfed until a month ago and did not have problems with attachment. He rolled at 4 months and has been able to sit independently since 8 months of age. His mother states that he can commando crawl but in a ‘crab like’ fashion in that he is propelling himself with his left side. He has developed a pincer grip in the left hand but the right hand is still grasping objects.

On examination his head circumference is 43cm (3rd centile), his weight and height are on the 50th centile. His BP is 90/70. He has no neurocutaneous stigmata and he is not dysmorphic. On inspection of his limbs you notice his right big toe is smaller than his left and his thumb on the right is also smaller than the left thumb. His tone is increased on the right side and his foot can only just get into a neutral position. There is sustained clonus at the right ankle. His power is only mildly reduced on the right side compared to the left in both the upper and lower limb. His reflexes are brisk with spread on the right but normal on the left. He is able to fix and follow, his facial movements are symmetrical and his voice is strong. He turns his head when you call his name.
